language.script_notes: Latin alphabet with the special letters þ (thorn) and ð (eth), plus á, é, í, ó, ú, ý, æ and ö. The letter ð appears in only one other European language, Faroese, so it is a strong tell but not a complete one. The internet domain is .is.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Yellow bollards, recognisable by their colour and their distinct top edge, are characteristic throughout the country.
road_furniture.line_paint: Some roads have white dashed edge markings, with grass often running right up to the road edge.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Yellow pedestrian-crossing signs appear, mainly in urban centres.

architecture.roof_style: Grass-covered turf roofs on traditional shelters (torfbæir), which protected people from the harsh climate for over a thousand years.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal on houses; turf on traditional farmhouses.
architecture.wall_construction: Modern buildings have large windows to maximise natural light and use little wood, because forestry resources are limited; classic timber lodges with small windows are absent; concrete and corrugated-metal-clad houses are common.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Turf-roofed farmhouses; brightly painted corrugated-metal houses; geothermal power plants and swimming pools; small white churches with red roofs.

nature.vegetation: Almost no vegetation other than grass — moss and needle grass dominate, and trees are scarce; only about 1% of the land is arable.
nature.terrain: Formed by lava and glaciers: the soil is black throughout, roads are mostly flat with undulating terrain and mountains in the distance, and rivers are irregular and braided with wetlands rather than straight-banked waterways.
nature.climate_signature: Cool, windy and often overcast, with long winters, glaciers and black volcanic sand.

vehicles.plate_color: White plates with no blue EU strip on the left.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: The Street View truck does not have the roof antenna seen on the Faroe Islands' vehicles.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The letter ð, similar Nordic North Atlantic landscapes, treeless green hills and sheep
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Faroese guardrails have yellow reflectors, found on no other northern European guardrails; the Faroes have long fjords with jagged green mountains rising straight out of the water, greener and more imposing than Iceland's; extra Faroese letters like Ø and Æ appear there.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Nordic language family, mountains and coast
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The letters þ and ð, yellow bollards and plates with no EU strip separate it; Norwegian uses å, ø and æ.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Arctic and subarctic scenery, glaciers and volcanic rock
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Icelandic text and road furniture with a much denser road network than Greenland's few connected towns.
